description: Exact-file migration ratchet. Token budgets may decrease; new legacy-brand occurrences fail.

allowedLines: # Design: Rename <legacy-title> to UIWitness
## Deliberate <legacy-title> Allowlist
- A migration/deprecation page that explicitly maps <legacy-title> to UIWitness.
- A third-party repository imports or invokes a published <legacy-title> package.
- Backward-compatibility and deprecation decisions for already-published <legacy-title> packages.

- Because this is a continuation of the same product and repository, release history remains continuous. The first UIWitness packages use version `0.25.0`, with repository `VERSION` set to `0.25.0.0`; prior <legacy-title> tags and changelog entries remain historical records.
- Existing `.<legacy-lower>/` evidence is untouched and remains gitignored.
- One approved inventory accounts for every <legacy-title> occurrence as renamed, historical, privacy-preserving, or compatibility-only.
- Privacy-safe treatment of existing `.<legacy-lower>/` evidence.
- The existing public <legacy-title> packages and executable need an intentional migration policy rather than silent abandonment.
- `.<legacy-lower>/` ignore rules and privacy-preservation tests.
1. Freeze a bridge inventory from the observed usage. The default inventory is only `<legacy-lower>-ui`; include an old supporting package only when evidence shows direct imports that need it.

2. Version every bridge package at `0.25.0` and tag the approved commit `<legacy-lower>-bridge-v0.25.0`. Keep the UIWitness repository release contract at `v0.25.0`; the distinct tag makes the legacy publication auditable.

4. Publish bridge dependencies first and `<legacy-lower>-ui` last through OIDC. The primary legacy executable forwards to the verified `uiwitness` package and emits one precise deprecation warning; it must not duplicate implementation.
6. Confirm package contents, terminal output, generated paths, JSON, and report UI contain no non-allowlisted <legacy-title> terminology.

<legacy-title> needs a distinct public identity before launch. An existing product already uses the <legacy-title> name for an overlapping frontend workflow built around product journeys, UI states, branches, and error paths. The current npm package `<legacy-lower>-ui` is valid and owned by this project, but npm ownership does not resolve the product-brand collision. The unrelated `<legacy-lower>` npm package and another CLI using a `<legacy-lower>` executable also make the current command identity harder to own.

Keep `schemaVersion: 1` and all current persisted fields unchanged. Rename the generated manifest filename to `uiwitness.json`, but ensure UIWitness report readers can open existing schema-v1 <legacy-title> payload fixtures. Rename public TypeScript symbols in the new packages. Do not add dual-name aliases to the new public API unless a verified external consumer requires them.

Maintain <legacy-title> aliases indefinitely alongside UIWitness. This doubles release, documentation, and support surfaces before meaningful adoption exists. A bounded bridge is permitted only if verified external use warrants it.

Market the product as UIWitness while retaining `<legacy-lower>-ui`, the `<legacy-lower>` executable, and `.<legacy-lower>/` artifacts. This is smaller but preserves the confusing identities users encounter during installation and support. It does not resolve the collision.
Rename the public product from <legacy-title> to **UIWitness** before its first broad announcement.
Repo: `RujitRaval/<legacy-lower>`

Retain `.<legacy-lower>/` in `.gitignore` and add `.uiwitness/`. The new CLI must never automatically rename, copy, upload, or delete `.<legacy-lower>/`; those directories may contain screenshots and sensitive application data. Migration guidance may tell users how to retain or remove their own artifacts deliberately.

The dated 2026-08-30 Gate 0 record narrows launch activity to the United States. The official USPTO wordmark search returned no live or dead exact `UIWitness` result. The maintainer approved `UIWitness`, confirmed that there are no known private or direct <legacy-title> consumers and no compatibility promises, and selected `deprecation-only`. No custom domain or launch-critical social handle is required; GitHub and npm are the canonical public destinations. The repository rename remains sequenced after the green implementation merge and immediately before publication, as defined below.

Use UIWitness consistently for the product, packages, executable, repository, generated files, artifacts, and documentation. Keep only explicit historical and migration references to <legacy-title>. Publish only after the pre-publication package-consumer gate passes; deprecate and announce only after the registry-only journey passes.
| A late trademark or identifier conflict | Treat clearance and control as blocking; keep <legacy-title> unchanged until passed |
| Config file | `<legacy-lower>.config.mts` | `uiwitness.config.mts` | New CLI does not silently mutate the old config | Check, promotion, configured scan |
| Docs and examples | <legacy-title> commands/imports/paths | UIWitness equivalents | Historical and migration references are allowlisted | Docs check and copy-paste smoke |

| Error codes and branded literals | <legacy-title>-prefixed values such as `<legacy-lower>.invalid` | UIWitness-prefixed equivalents | Rename only values outside the frozen persisted schema; document any persisted legacy value | Error snapshots and legacy-report fixtures |
| Evidence root | `.<legacy-lower>/` | `.uiwitness/` | Keep both gitignored; never auto-migrate or delete old evidence | Ignore checks and pre-existing-directory fixture |
| Executable | `<legacy-lower>` | `uiwitness` | Forwarding legacy CLI only if external-use threshold is met | `--help`, PATH resolution, old-package smoke if required |

| Exported TypeScript API | `<legacy-title>*` symbols | `UIWitness*` symbols | New packages expose only the new names; old packages remain frozen unless bridge triggered | API extraction/types consumer fixture |
| GitHub repository | `RujitRaval/<legacy-lower>` | `RujitRaval/uiwitness` | Rename immediately before first new-package release | Redirect, clone, issues, releases, links |

| Internal identifiers | Values such as `<legacy-lower>:public-site`, package scopes, generated imports | UIWitness equivalents | Inventory every match; exceptions require allowlist entry | Case-insensitive source/build/package search |
| Manifest filename | `.<legacy-lower>/report/<legacy-lower>.json` | `.uiwitness/report/uiwitness.json` | Filename changes; payload remains schema v1 | Golden fixtures and report opening |
| Primary package | `<legacy-lower>-ui` | `uiwitness` | No alias in the new package | Registry metadata and clean install |
| Product prose | <legacy-title> | UIWitness | Old name appears only in the allowlist below | Repository and rendered-doc search |
| Scenario root | `<legacy-lower>/scenarios/` | `uiwitness/scenarios/` | Explicit migration guidance; no silent move | Fixture and consumer-smoke assertions |
| Scripts and environment names | <legacy-title>-branded names | UIWitness-branded names | Rename public and release-facing identifiers; avoid unrelated churn | CI and release rehearsal |
| Supporting packages | `<legacy-lower>-ui-*` | `uiwitness-*` | Preserve dependency graph; publish primary last | Packed manifests and registry dependency resolution |
| Tags, changelog, ADRs | Historical <legacy-title> record | Preserved verbatim where historically necessary | Do not rewrite history | Allowlist-audited search |
+--> accepts legacy .<legacy-lower>/ screenshot paths
.<legacy-lower>/**  --> never read, moved, copied, or deleted by a new run
.<legacy-lower>/artifacts/... --> accepted --> href relative to .<legacy-lower> report
.<legacy-lower>/artifacts/... --> type/runtime rejection
- An existing `.<legacy-lower>/**` tree is byte-identical before and after successful, failed, and interrupted UIWitness runs.
- Existing `.<legacy-lower>/` coexistence and privacy cases.
- Implementation-only literals such as `<legacy-lower>.invalid`, `<legacy-lower>IssueCode`, and `<legacy-lower>:public-site`.

- Instrumented filesystem sentinels observe zero `open`, `read`, `stat`, `readdir`, `realpath`, or traversal calls beneath `.<legacy-lower>/**` during check, scan, open, success, failure, interruption, and recovery flows.
- New HTML contains UIWitness identity and no non-allowlisted <legacy-title> text.
- Prove the documented manual process leaves `.<legacy-lower>/**` untouched unless the user explicitly copies files.
- Public type names such as `<legacy-title>Config`, `<legacy-title>Scenario`, `<legacy-title>Report`, `<legacy-title>Error`, and `<legacy-title>ErrorCode` to their `UIWitness*` forms.

- [x] **T2 (P1, human: ~1 day / Codex: ~45 min)**: Brand contract: add the executable <legacy-title> allowlist and CI/release gate. Implemented with an exact-file migration ratchet, strict exact-line rules for both rename records, root lint/CI enforcement, and a strict pre-publication release check that rejects migration-only entries.
- `<legacy-lower>-ui has moved to uiwitness. Install uiwitness and migrate with https://github.com/RujitRaval/uiwitness/blob/main/docs/open-source/MIGRATING_TO_UIWITNESS.md`
- `<legacy-lower>-ui-core has moved to uiwitness-core. Install uiwitness-core and migrate with https://github.com/RujitRaval/uiwitness/blob/main/docs/open-source/MIGRATING_TO_UIWITNESS.md`
- `<legacy-lower>-ui-report has moved to uiwitness-report. Install uiwitness-report and migrate with https://github.com/RujitRaval/uiwitness/blob/main/docs/open-source/MIGRATING_TO_UIWITNESS.md`

- `<legacy-lower>-ui-runner-playwright has moved to uiwitness-runner-playwright. Install uiwitness-runner-playwright and migrate with https://github.com/RujitRaval/uiwitness/blob/main/docs/open-source/MIGRATING_TO_UIWITNESS.md`
- `apps/example-nextjs/<legacy-lower>.config.ts` to `uiwitness.config.ts`.
- `apps/example-nextjs/<legacy-lower>/scenarios/` to `uiwitness/scenarios/`.
- `packages/core/src/results.ts` parses valid `.uiwitness/artifacts/**` and legacy `.<legacy-lower>/artifacts/**` read paths before transformation.
15. Classify intentional historical <legacy-title> text in the approved rename design and this engineering plan through narrow path-plus-pattern brand rules.
2. Keep `schemaVersion: 1`. New writers emit only `.uiwitness/`; report readers accept both `.uiwitness/` and legacy `.<legacy-lower>/` screenshot paths.

3. Keep <legacy-title> aliases and the `<legacy-lower>` executable entirely inside these wrappers. Each wrapper forwards exports without adding behavior. The CLI wrapper forwards arguments and exit status to `uiwitness` while printing one deprecation warning to stderr per process.
3. Never automatically rename, copy, upload, or delete an existing `.<legacy-lower>/` directory.
4. Allow only historical tags/releases/changelog/accepted decisions, the migration page, old-package deprecation metadata, `.<legacy-lower>/` ignore/privacy tests, and an approved legacy bridge.

5. Publish through `.github/workflows/release-legacy-bridge.yml`, a separate protected `npm-legacy-bridge` environment, dependency-first order, OIDC trusted-publisher subjects rebound to the renamed repository, and tag `<legacy-lower>-bridge-v0.25.0`.
Add both `.<legacy-lower>/` and `.uiwitness/` to `.gitignore`. The docs checker must ignore both sensitive evidence roots.
Do not add <legacy-title> aliases to the new public packages. If the bridge gate is triggered, compatibility lives in a separate legacy package inventory, not in the UIWitness public API.

Rename the product, public packages, executable, generated project files, evidence paths, current documentation, release automation, and launch assets from <legacy-title> to UIWitness before public announcement.
